summary:
plan.md is written for four flat-roofed blocks set on their real footprints. All 20 masses were checked against the footprint maps and fit. Ground floors step down the slope, with plinths down to the ground and the walls stepping in jogs to follow the street's slant.
Economy has red brick, cream terracotta trim, an arched glass doorway off Pike Street and a glowing skylight (its tallest point, y 42-44). Corner has three brick storeys with big arches over striped-awning stalls and white-framed windows. Sanitary is a long cream two-storey front of open stalls under red and green awnings with SANITARY PUBLIC MARKET lettering. Garden Center is small brick with a fire escape.
Upper walls stand one block inside the street edges and shopfronts sit three in, so awnings, letters and lanterns stay on the footprint. Light behind glass and in the stalls carries the dusk render. Not built or rendered yet; small footprint slivers are left empty. Four brick and stucco market buildings built to their real site orientation. Each wall runs down to the ground, and the arches, awnings, banner signs, skylight and fire escape are built block by block. Lit stalls, shroomlight-backed windows and lanterns give the dusk glow.
Six parts: three shell and roof parts (Economy; Corner; Sanitary with Garden Center), two facade-fitting parts, and one for stalls, lights and grounds.
elements.md and the plan.md PALETTE, VOCABULARY, ROOMS and PARTS sections are written. All block ids passed `mcd blocks --check`. The VOCABULARY helpers (26) are specified but untested against the toolkit, and the street and entrance cells are unwalked.
elements: Sanitary and Garden shell and roof (parts/sanitary-garden.mjs)

summary: Economy shell and roof: parts/economy.mjs builds the Economy Market shell on its ground (E1–E5 as one hollow brick mass with a stone plinth, openings, floors, roof decks, cornice and parapets). It also builds the E5 atrium doorway frame, the E6 skylight on a curb, the E2 name panel base and lantern flagpole, and the E4 terrace rail and planter. make.sh finishes with a whole build.nbt and no refused writes. I did not run `$MCD fit`, did not view the renders, and did not read the `$MCD check` output.
polish: Not verified: `$MCD check` output was filtered and not read, `$MCD fit` wasn't run, and the render produced no tiles (that command's output was discarded), so nothing was looked at.
No quoins and no brick piers every 6 on the east faces; the east wall is plain brick with a string course at y26 and a cornice.
Roof decks are laid by hand with a stone_bricks/polished_andesite checker; no roof.json was written.
The east masses are trimmed one cell so the wall plane is edge-1. Edge cells (x 56/53/50) are free for awnings and banners, except that my cornice stairs sit at y33..34 there.

The E5 atrium has a glass fan at y16..20, a stair arch at y21 and a quartz keystone at y22. The stepped cream pediment above y26 is only the parapet ring; there are no lanterns and no ECONOMY banner letters.
The E2 tall window is a rectangular opening (z4..7, y28..33) with a sandstone head. It is not a true arch.
The E4 arched windows and the west-face windows are rectangular air openings, and no glazing has been added to any window.
Windows whose lowest row would sit at or under the ground were dropped, so some west rows are missing where the bluff is high.
The skylight void is x24..40, z20..30 at y35, with a stone curb around it at x23/41 and z19/31. Floors at y26 and above are left open under it.

waste.what: Derived wall cells for six masses that share edges: the exposed-neighbour rule, per-face trims and the opening boxes were all worked out by hand. plinthTo fills solid up to wallY, so I couldn't use it.
waste.cost: about 100 lines of custom code, one failed first write
waste.tool: a vocab helper `massShell(g, masses, openings, groundAt)` that walls the union of masses and keeps window boxes as air

waste.what: Spaced window boxes along each face by hand, one loop per face.
waste.cost: about 10 loops
waste.tool: a `bayRows(face, start, step, rows)` window generator driven by the OPENINGS table

companions.task: Quoins, piers every 6 on the east face, and the true arches for the E2 window and the E4 annex windows.
Glass panes and frames for every opening I left as air, and lit backing blocks for the glass.

summary:
Corner shell and roof: P2 Corner shell built in parts/corner.mjs: C1-C4 walls down to ground with stone plinth, brick walls, quoins, floors at y16/y24, deck at y32, cornice at y31, parapet (brick 33, coping 34), two chimney stacks and the stair house.
Arch bays and upper window cells are left unplaced for P4 to carve and glaze. make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; the Corner part reports 0 refused and 0 off-palette.
Not done: no roof.json (the roof is a deck plus parapet, not the roof tool), and the projecting quoins at the east corners are flagged as orphans by check.
polish: No roof.json: the flat roof is a hand-placed deck (stone_bricks/polished_andesite checker at y32) with a parapet, not a roof-tool roof with trusses or overhang. Add roof.json if the roof part wants it.
Arch openings (floor+1..15) and 2nd/3rd storey window cells (y18-22, y26-30) are left unplaced for P4 to carve (archOpening) and glaze (windowFrame/litWindow); P4 must place into them.
Quoins at the east corners (x=112, z=30 and the others) project one cell into the edge band and show as ORPHAN in mcd check; intended as projections but unverified against P4's awnings and banners.
Upper-window placement on the C1 north face and the uphill east faces is approximate (every 8, offset 3..4); not matched to a designed bay grid.
Interior stall rooms are air only (no fittings); P6 furnishes them. The stair house has no door cell placed beyond the helper's default.

Visual check was partial: I read a north zoom and the street tile; the corner-only render failed (cropping by setting air over the whole grid ran out of memory), so the west faces were not checked by eye.

waste.what: Wrote the wall, floor and deck placement cell by cell for four rectangular masses, including the plinth, mossy variant and opening skips
waste.cost: one generator loop, about 13.6k blocks set; two runs of make.sh to fix window positions
waste.tool: a massShell(g, {x0,x1,z0,z1,floor,ground,openings}) helper in the build library or vocab: ring walls, interior air, floor courses, plinth to floor level, string course, with an openings callback

waste.what: Worked out opening and window spans (arch bays 6 wide, windows at offsets 0-1 and 4-5, corner-safe offsets) by hand for each street and side face
waste.cost: about six coordinate lists computed by hand; one bug (north windows on the quoin cells, then east windows on the corner cells) found only through mcd check
waste.tool: plan detail in plan.md giving window offsets per bay (a bay grid with start cells) instead of the rhythm text; or a helper bayWindows(span, offsets)

waste.what: Tried to isolate the Corner plot for a close render by setting air over the rest of the grid cell by cell
waste.cost: one run that ran out of memory (about 4 GB heap), then a fallback to the full render tiles
waste.tool: mcd crop build.nbt --box x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1 (or a box filter on render/zoom) to view one plot without rewriting the grid

waste.what: Chose the cornice box and face by reading the helper's source (outer column = the box edge) and tried it on each face
waste.cost: one read of cornice() source, then one build to confirm placement
waste.tool: cornice's doc comment stating the column it lands on (wall plane or the edge band) and an example call

companions.task: carve the six round arch bays on the west and south faces of C1-C4 (floor+1 to 15, 6 wide, spring at floor+5, crown at 15) with the brick_stairs arch and smooth_sandstone keystones and imposts, and the quoins that line them.
lay the flat roof properly: a roof.json for the deck at y32 with the stone_bricks and polished_andesite mix, parapet coping and scuppers, instead of my hand-placed deck.
finish the two chimney stacks and the stair house cap: the deepslate band at y36, the slab caps at 37-38, and the door at z60.

summary: Sanitary and Garden shell and roof: placeholder
polish: No cornice on any Sanitary or Garden mass (plan: cornice y22 and Garden y14); the flat roofs have plain parapets only.
No sanitaryPier pier caps: the piers are the solid ring between openings, with cut_sandstone courses at y10 and y13 but no separate pier heads.
Garden north door sits at y4..5, not y3..4: the ground under (230,2) is 3, so y3 is stone. Plan.md Notes need this line.
Sanitary east and north faces have no windows and no plinth course (plan asks for both).
Window and shopfront surrounds are framed only on the Sanitary west upper windows and the entrance; Garden shopfronts and north windows are unframed (left for P5).
Garden G1 and G2 roof deck and parapet only; roof plants are P6's job.
Check flags from other parts (9 floating shroomlight cells at 32,34,21..29 and two orphan bricks at 56,33,4/6) are not in this part.

waste.what: Worked out every opening, window and frame cell by hand from the plan (z starts per mass, y ranges, the Garden door offset) and wrote each carve as a loop.
waste.cost: about 40 min of coordinate reasoning; several passes to fix the ring/inset boxes at mass junctions
waste.tool: a `massShell` helper in vocab taking the box, floor, frieze and ceiling courses, and an `openings` list per face that carves and frames in one call, so a part states only the openings and not the cells

waste.what: Checked the look of the west face by eye from zoom tiles, one pass.
waste.cost: 2 zoom renders, 1 render

companions.task: The cornice courses (smooth_sandstone stairs upside down with brick dentils) on every Sanitary mass and the Garden cornice at y14, plus the pier caps at y10.
Roof parapet and decks: the checker deck, the parapet coping and the vent lids, checked against the roof spec so the decks match the roof tool's output.
Window and shopfront glazing and surrounds for P5: the Garden shopfronts at x214 and the north windows, which this part carves but does not frame.

summary:
Economy and Corner facade fittings: Part 4 (parts/economy-corner-facade.mjs) built: Economy street-storey shop windows and upper windows with glass, a striped awning over each street run, E2 arched window and ECONOMY/MARKET name block; Corner round arches (west x78/72/66, south z94/100), two-storey window pairs on both faces, and the CORNER MARKET panel.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; P4 ticked in plan.md and its elements.md items.
Atrium doorway and its ECONOMY band are left to the Economy shell, which already builds the fan, arch and band.
polish: OFF-PALETTE: bannerWord writes red_wall_banner/white_wall_banner (24 cells across ECONOMY, MARKET and CORNER MARKET), which palette.json does not list. Needs *_wall_banner added to the palette or the lettering swapped to palette blocks.

Structure warnings that belong to the parallel parts: the Corner shell is not built in this copy (corner.mjs is a stub), so the Corner windows float and the CORNER MARKET banners hang on air. Re-check once the Corner shell lands.
Corner arch-mouth awnings and the open produce stalls behind the arches are not built (stripedAwning would write off the footprint at edge+1); needs a local in-place awning like the Economy one.
Quoins are not built: quoins replaces the shell's brick, which runParts refuses.
Atrium lettering (ECONOMY on the z59 cream band) is not built: the shell has the band as smooth_sandstone, so the letters need to go in front of it or the shell needs to leave the band as air.
Shroomlight orphans at x54 in the Economy shop rooms (lit windows touch the build on one face); harmless for a glow, but flagged by check.
Visual check: the front-right tile shows the whole module with the Corner missing, so the facade could not be judged by eye yet.

waste.what: Economy awnings: stripedAwning steps its back course to edge+1, which is off the footprint, so I wrote each awning cell by cell with g.set.
waste.cost: about 40 g.set calls worked out by hand
waste.tool: An awning helper that takes the edge cell (no outward step) and writes wool plus the trapdoor valance, or a stripedAwning option such as {outward:0}.

waste.what: Banner lettering: bannerWord writes *_wall_banner ids that palette.json does not list, so every letter is OFF-PALETTE.
waste.cost: 24 banner cells, plus a palette report to read and a plan note to write
waste.tool: A palette entry for the wall-banner variants (red_wall_banner, white_wall_banner), or a bannerWord option that letters in palette blocks such as wool or concrete.

waste.what: Window and arch coordinates worked out by hand from the plan's bay rhythm (arch centres at z35/43/51, z59/67/75, x71/79, x91/99, windows at bay start and +4).
waste.cost: about 15 coordinate sets computed by hand, then one check run to confirm
waste.tool: A bay helper that takes a face, a plane coordinate and the arch bays from plan.md's OPENINGS table and emits archOpening, windowFrame and litWindow calls together.

waste.what: Checking that litWindow and windowFrame position their cells: the at-point convention is not documented, so I relied on the placed count and the render.
waste.cost: 2 build runs and a render to confirm
waste.tool: A one-line note in vocab/h1.mjs and h2.mjs on which corner of the opening at refers to on each face.

companions.task: Shape the arch shoulders and keystones on the Corner's round arches (archOpening gives a plain 6-wide arch) and the cream terracotta trim around them.
Lay out CORNER MARKET and the Economy ECONOMY/MARKET lettering at the correct letter size and reading direction, in palette blocks.
Set the Corner's window frames, sills and the shroomlight behind each pane so the glass reads warm at dusk, and fit the Economy's valances properly.

summary:
Sanitary and Garden facade fittings: Built parts/sanitary-garden-facade.mjs (P5): Sanitary west-face canopies in the edge band, six shop fascia signs, SANITARY PUBLIC MARKET and second SANITARY lettering, entrance jambs, lit upper windows on each step, Garden shopfronts with a top-slab lintel, green/white canopies, GARDEN CENTER lettering, window boxes, Post Alley door and lit windows, fire escape, PLANTS hanging sign.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; P5 places 911 blocks with no refusals; check and fit pass on this part alone.
Ticked P5 in plan.md and five elements.md items; appended a P5 note to plan.md's Notes.
polish: OFF-PALETTE: bannerWord's letter cloth is white_wall_banner (x40, base "white"); palette.json lists only standing white_banner. Add the wall-banner ids to the palette or accept the banner-word object.
Window frames not applied: Sanitary upper windows (y16..18) and Garden upper windows (x212, y9..12) are lit panes with no white quartz frame; the Sanitary entrance frame is only the jambs and lintel.
Sanitary hanging blade signs not built: the edge-band canopy at y8..9 is in the way. Only the Garden PLANTS hanging sign exists.
Garden door sits at y4 (ground 3 under it), not the plan's y3..4; only the lower cell of the second half is at x230, not the plan's x230..231.

Sanitary shop fascia signs at y11 (x128, z84/92/100/122/130/138) and the lettering at y12 need the frieze wall from P3 behind them; the test build had no shell, so their support is unverified until merge.
Garden GARDEN CENTER lettering is one row at y16 in front of the panel at x212; the cream panel itself is P3's.
Window boxes are slab plus potted_fern at x211 y8..9 (the plan's gardenPot trapdoor design failed fit); P6 owns gardenPot planting.
Check and fit were run on the part alone with no shell: the floating and unsupported warnings were artefacts of the missing walls; fit passes. Not verified against the merged shell.

waste.what: Figured out by reading helper source that stripedAwning steps the course out past the footprint edge (edge+o), so it would stand off the footprint; wrote a local canopy() in the edge column instead.
waste.cost: one read of h2.mjs plus a rewrite of the awning call sites
waste.tool: stripedAwning option to stay inside the footprint edge band (edge column only), or a canopy helper in vocab

waste.what: bannerWord's cloth is a dye colour, so every banner cell becomes <colour>_wall_banner; the palette only lists standing banners, so the build reports 40 OFF-PALETTE cells I could not avoid without dropping the lettering.
waste.cost: one make.sh cycle to see it, then a palette/plan note
waste.tool: palette.json needs the wall-banner ids (or a palette-aware bannerWord), and a lettering helper that reports which banner ids it uses

waste.what: shopFront's lintel is a bottom slab, so the fascia planks above it float on air; fit flagged 20 cells and I overrode the lintel row by hand.
waste.cost: one fit cycle and a 20-cell loop
waste.tool: shopFront option for the lintel slab type (top) or a lintel row built as a top slab

waste.what: gardenPot box variant puts a potted plant on an open trapdoor, which fit rejects (a plant needs a top face); replaced by a top slab with a fern, by hand per cell.
waste.cost: one fit cycle and per-cell placement for 6 window-box cells
waste.tool: a window-box helper (slab or trapdoor on the wall line plus a plant on a full top) that passes fit

waste.what: Upper-window bays placed by hand (z loop every 4 along each step's plane) and the window frames not applied: windowFrame needs the shell's wall to be registered against, which this copy does not have.
waste.cost: about 20 litWindow calls written by a loop, frames not placed
waste.tool: facadeBays(g, {plane, z0, z1, every, at, w, h, lit}) that takes the shell's wall plane from the plan's mass table, plus a frame option

waste.what: Rendering the part gave nothing to judge: the shell is in another copy, so the tiles show only the Economy shell and loose fittings. Structure warnings (floating awnings, unsupported signs, orphan jambs) all come from the missing wall.
waste.cost: two render passes and an eye check I could not make meaningful
waste.tool: render the part on the merged shell (or a shell fixture from the plan's mass table) instead of alone

companions.task: the SANITARY PUBLIC MARKET and GARDEN CENTER lettering: the letter cloth colours and the cream board behind them, plus the six shop fascia boards on the frieze
the white quartz window frames on the Sanitary upper bays and the Garden upper windows, the entrance jambs, and the shopfront glass lines (so the frames are placed, not just the lit panes)

companions.role: awning maker (canvas and wool stripe awnings)
companions.task: the stripe run and the valance on the Sanitary edge band and the Garden canopies, so the canopy stands out from the wall and the stripes keep their colour order across the run

summary:
Stalls, lights and grounds: parts/stalls-lights.mjs fills the stall rooms (Economy street band, Corner C1-C3 and C3 south, Sanitary S1/S1s/S1b/S6, Garden shops A and B) with stallFit, puts street lamps on each Pike Place face's footprint edge (read from the footprint map), and adds the Corner arch-crown lanterns, two E4 terrace planters, a Garden roof planter and three Garden window boxes.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; my part places 2558 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette. Light in the stall rooms reads 8+ at most cells (the Corner C3 and Garden rooms run lower near the back).
The render is mostly the other parts' work so far; I did not check my lamps and stalls by eye at close range.
polish: Economy atrium stall (box [43,13,49,46,25,58]) is not built: no stall front fits the atrium's 4-wide floor, and no produceCrate was placed in its place.
Sanitary S2..S5 stalls and the S1 entrance hall are not built: ROOMS in plan.md gives no box for them.
Bracket lanterns (lanternBracket) at pier heads are not built.
Corner arch-crown lanterns use hand-picked arch centres (79,35/43/51 and 71,59/67/75) at y14; they were not checked against the built arch keystones, so some may be refused once P2/P4 merge.
Garden window boxes (gardenPot box) on the x211 edge and the Garden roof planter (y16..17) float in this isolated build because the Garden shell (P3) is not merged; they should sit once it is.
Economy E4 planters and the lamp posts rest on ground cells; not verified against the merged Economy roof (no roof.json yet).
I did not verify the lamps and stalls by eye at close range; the street render only shows the unmerged shells.

waste.what: Worked out the stall rooms, lamp positions and planter boxes one by one from plan.md's ROOMS and the footprint map, and found the C3 stall overlap by hand.
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of reading and coordinate checks before the first make.sh run
waste.tool: A rooms file in the kit (rooms.json filled from plan.md ROOMS) so `mcd room`/`mcd light` can run per stall; a helper that finds each Pike Place face's edge cell from the footprint map and places a lamp on it.

waste.what: Checked each stall room's light level by reading the `mcd light` output for every room separately, with a scratch rooms file I wrote myself.
waste.cost: one scratch rooms file and one command
waste.tool: rooms.json for this part should be filled from plan.md ROOMS, so `mcd light build.nbt --rooms rooms.json` gives every room at once.

waste.what: Checked the render by eye from a street tile where the other parts are not yet merged, so the tile shows the shells only.
waste.cost: one render and one look
waste.tool: A render that can be run after the parts are merged, or a tile limited to the part's own cells (`mcd zoom --at`).

companions.task: Place the Corner arch-crown lanterns and the Sanitary pier brackets against the merged keystones and piers, and set the light levels in the Economy atrium and the Sanitary S2..S5 stalls.
Plant the Economy E4 terrace and the Garden Center roof, and place the window boxes once the Garden shell is in place.
Fit the Economy atrium stall with its counters (it is 4 wide, so it needs a different front from the street band).

summary: inspection: Fixed the fit issues at their source: stall goods now stand on full spruce planks (vocab/h1.mjs stallFit), and the Sanitary lettering gets a sandstone support under each standing banner (parts/sanitary-garden-facade.mjs). Walk was already ok and is unchanged. make.sh rebuilt build.nbt; walk ok, fit OK.

waste.what: The fit report listed 9 of 131 issues and cut the rest, so I inferred the pattern from the stall helper source instead of reading it from the report.
waste.cost: One grep of vocab/h1.mjs to find the bottom slab under goods, about 3 tool calls.
waste.tool: fit should print the cause pattern (goods on the counter slab at every even front cell, stallFit) and the full list or a per-helper count.

waste.what: The CHEESE shop board sat under the banner letter at 128,12,122, which the first fit output did not show; found only after a rebuild.
waste.cost: One rebuild, a second fit run, and one edit to move the board.
waste.tool: fit could list every issue with its helper or part name, and flag a banner over a non-solid block as the same class.
